AI.method: Compare four products (GHSL, TEMPO, GBA, Overture) against ORBITaL-Net footprints. Assess on grids of multiple spatial resolutions using conventional metrics (e.g., perhaps precision, recall, F1, IoU). Stratify results by geographic region, population density, and income levels to analyze context-dependent performance.
AI.result: GBA or TEMPO generally achieve the highest accuracy, depending on evaluation criteria. Accuracy varies by geography, population density, and income; all products perform significantly worse in Africa and Asia, and most show reduced accuracy in high-density urban areas.
AI.conclusion: No single product dominates across all contexts; independent, multi-resolution evaluation reveals context-dependent strengths and weaknesses. The choice of raster dataset should consider region and urban density, and there is a need for targeted improvements in Africa/Asia and dense urban settings.

title: Predictive single cell foundation model for gene regulation and aging with privacy-preserving tabular learning
comment: 98 pages, 4 main figures, and 15 supplementary figures
summary: Pre-trained foundation models (FMs) have begun transforming single-cell genomics, but scaling them raises privacy concerns. Moreover, unlike text data, single-cell data is unordered and exhibits a unique tabular structure that current single-cell FMs overlook. We introduce Tabula, a privacy-preserving FM designed with federated learning (FL) that explicitly models the tabular structure of single-cell data. To deploy Tabula, we further developed Chiron, a decentralized AI agent-enabled platform for collaborative training across institutions without sharing raw data. Beyond strong performance across downstream benchmarks, Tabula reveals combinatorial regulatory logic across diverse biological systems, including hematopoiesis, pancreatic endogenesis, neurogenesis, and cardiogenesis. Using a new scRNA-seq dataset of paired young and aged human fibroblasts, Tabula nominates rejuvenation factors through age- and identity score-guided in silico prioritization, outperforming conventional approaches. Thus, Tabula represents an important advance in single-cell foundation modeling by integrating tabular learning with FL, paving the way toward privacy-preserving virtual cells for human health.

AI.tldr: Tabula is a privacy-preserving single-cell foundation model that treats scRNA-seq data as tabular and leverages federated learning to enable cross-institution training, with a decentralized platform Chiron for collaboration; it delivers strong benchmarks, uncovers combinatorial regulatory logic across multiple developmental systems, and prioritizes rejuvenation factors in aged fibroblasts.
AI.motivation: Single-cell data poses privacy risks and has a distinct tabular/unordered structure not well captured by existing foundation models. The work aims to enable scalable, privacy-preserving foundation modeling for single-cell genomics by integrating tabular learning with federated training and enabling cross-institution collaboration.
AI.method: Develop Tabula, a tabular-structure-aware foundation model trained via federated learning to preserve privacy. Deploy Chiron, a decentralized AI agent-enabled platform that coordinates collaborative training across institutions without sharing raw data. Evaluate on diverse biological systems (hematopoiesis, pancreatic endogenesis, neurogenesis, cardiogenesis) and new scRNA-seq dataset of paired young/aged fibroblasts, using age- and identity-guided in silico prioritization.
AI.result: Tabula achieves strong performance on downstream benchmarks, reveals combinatorial regulatory logic across systems, and nominates rejuvenation factors in aged fibroblasts that outperform conventional methods.
AI.conclusion: Integrating tabular learning with federated training advances single-cell foundation modeling and privacy-preserving collaboration, enabling 'virtual cells' for human health and enabling cross-institution studies.

title: Unified Prediction and Planning via Conflict-Aware Disjoint Parameter Training
comment: Accepted at ECCV 2026. 38 pages, 14 figures. Project page: https://dpt2026.github.io/
summary: Accurate motion prediction of surrounding agents and safe motion planning are two closely coupled key tasks for social robot navigation in crowded environments. Deploying these systems on resource-constrained edge devices necessitates compact, unified models that can perform both tasks simultaneously. However, within these compact shared encoders, recent unified models often overlook severe representational conflicts that arise from the distinct objectives of predicting neighbor behaviors versus ego-centric safety planning. To address this issue, we first identify the Skill Conflict$\unicode{x2014}$a phenomenon where overlapping parameter assignments cause distinct tasks to compete for the same weights, preventing the model from fully specializing in individual skills. To resolve this, we propose a novel model-merging-based framework, Disjoint Parameter Training (DPT). DPT mitigates performance degradation caused by Skill Conflict through distributed parameter learning, which separates the key parameter regions of each task while preserving their core capabilities prior to merging. In addition, we observe that sparse merging, which selectively integrates only the most influential parameters for each task rather than combining all task-specific parameters, yields optimal performance by preventing interference among adjacent features and concentrating representational capacity. DPT can be applied in parallel with a variety of merging methods. Evaluated on standard crowd navigation benchmarks (JRDB and JTA), our framework demonstrates superior performance, validating its versatility and effectiveness for safe, resource-efficient robot navigation.

AI.tldr: A unified, resource-efficient motion prediction and planning model can suffer Skill Conflict in shared encoders; the paper introduces Disjoint Parameter Training (DPT) with sparse merging to separate task-specific parameters before merging, improving performance on crowd-navigation benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Need for accurate yet resource-efficient joint motion prediction and safety planning on edge devices. Shared encoders can cause representational conflicts because neighbor-behavior prediction and ego-safety planning have different objectives, hindering specialization.
AI.method: Identify Skill Conflict; propose Disjoint Parameter Training (DPT) to distribute parameter learning and separate key parameter regions per task prior to merging. Employ sparse merging to integrate only the most influential task-specific parameters, reducing interference. DPT is compatible with multiple merging methods and can run in parallel.
AI.result: On standard crowd navigation benchmarks JRDB and JTA, the DPT-based framework demonstrates superior performance, validating its effectiveness and versatility for safe, resource-efficient robot navigation.
AI.conclusion: DPT with sparse merging mitigates interference from shared encoders, enabling task specialization within a unified model while preserving core capabilities; the framework is versatile across merging methods and suitable for resource-constrained social navigation.

title: Euclean: Automated Geometry Problem Formalization with Unified Verification in Lean
summary: Recent formal reasoning systems have reached IMO-level performance, yet they leave a fragmented landscape: algebra and number theory are handled in Lean, while geometry still relies on domain-specific languages with limited formal guarantees. This split increases the trusted computing base and hinders unified model development. Existing geometry-in-Lean efforts (LeanEuclid, LeanGeo) introduce custom axiom systems incompatible with standard Mathlib, and their small scale ($<$ 1,100 problems) limits large-scale training. Native Mathlib autoformalization of geometry, however, poses distinct challenges: implicit diagrammatic assumptions (e.g., topological configuration and non-degeneracy) must be made explicit rather than deferred to external solvers, and models must adapt to Mathlib's small, rapidly evolving geometry infrastructure. We present Euclean, a four-stage framework - constraint explication, configuration anchoring, formalization mapping, and iterative repair - for automatically formalizing geometry in native Mathlib. We construct OMNI-Geometry (768 competition problems) and Numina-Geometry (177,597 problems), the largest geometry formalization dataset in Lean. Human evaluation shows 48.89% TOP1 and 73.33% TOP5 accuracy. Training Goedel v2 on our formalizations improves proof success from 13.6% to 15.1%, validating dataset quality for unified neural theorem proving. Code and datasets: https://github.com/tlb-22/Euclean.

AI.tldr: A four-stage pipeline (constraint explication, configuration anchoring, formalization mapping, iterative repair) to auto-formalize geometry in native Mathlib, producing the largest Lean geometry datasets (OMNI-Geometry and Numina-Geometry) and enabling improved neural theorem proving.
AI.motivation: Address fragmentation in Lean geometry formalization, align geometry with Mathlib, and provide large-scale data for training and evaluation of automated and neural theorem proving.
AI.method: Four-stage pipeline: (1) constraint explication of implicit diagrammatic assumptions, (2) configuration anchoring to Mathlib's geometry infrastructure, (3) formalization mapping into Lean, and (4) iterative repair to resolve inconsistencies. Dataset construction yields OMNI-Geometry (768 problems) and Numina-Geometry (177,597 problems). Human evaluation and neural prover experiments validate dataset quality and utility. Code and data are released.
AI.result: Human evaluation shows TOP1 accuracy 48.89% and TOP5 accuracy 73.33%. Training Goedel v2 on the formalizations increases proof success from 13.6% to 15.1%, demonstrating dataset utility for unified neural theorem proving.
AI.conclusion: Euclean enables native Mathlib geometry formalization at scale, delivering the largest Lean geometry corpus and supporting improved neural theorem proving; code and datasets are publicly available for reproducibility and further research.

title: DRGBT-1K: A Large-scale High-quality Benchmark for Dynamic RGBT Tracking
summary: Dynamic RGBT (DRGBT) tracking aims to continuously localize a target when the available sensing modalities and observation platforms vary over time. Compared with conventional RGBT tracking with fixed RGBT inputs and a fixed observation platform, DRGBT tracking is more consistent with real-world collaborative perception systems, where targets may be observed by heterogeneous sensors from different viewpoints. However, existing benchmarks are still insufficient for systematically evaluating tracker robustness under real dynamic modality variations and cross-platform transitions. To address this limitation, we make the following contributions. 1) We construct DRGBT-1K, a large-scale high-quality benchmark for DRGBT tracking. It contains 1,045 sequences captured entirely in real-world scenarios and 795K RGBT frame pairs collected using UAVs and handheld RGBT devices, encompassing diverse real-world scenes, pronounced viewpoint changes, modality variations, and target appearance discontinuities. 2) We provide comprehensive annotations for fine-grained evaluation, including dense bounding boxes, target category labels, challenge attributes, frame-level modality labels and platform labels. DRGBT-1K covers 24 target categories, more than 15 scene types and 15 challenge attributes. 3) We establish a comprehensive benchmark by evaluating 20 representative multimodal tracking methods, including conventional RGBT trackers, modality-missing RGBT trackers, and DRGBT trackers under a unified evaluation protocol. 4) We release an unaligned version of DRGBT-1K and derive UGVT-1K to support broader research on unaligned multimodal tracking and UAV-ground collaborative tracking. 5) We develop an online evaluation platform for DRGBT-1K and provide a leaderboard that collects all methods evaluated on this benchmark.

AI.tldr: Introduces DRGBT-1K, a large-scale real-world benchmark for dynamic RGBT tracking, with 1,045 sequences and 795K RGBT frame pairs from UAVs and handheld devices; provides detailed annotations; evaluates 20 trackers; offers unaligned UGVT-1K and an online leaderboard.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks do not adequately capture tracker robustness under time-varying modalities and cross-platform transitions in real-world multimodal perception systems; there is a need for systematic evaluation of dynamic RGBT tracking under modality and platform changes.
AI.method: Construction of DRGBT-1K by collecting 1,045 real-world sequences and 795K RGBT frame pairs from UAVs and handheld RGBT devices; dense bounding boxes, target category labels, 15 challenge attributes, frame-level modality labels and platform labels; 24 target categories, 15 scene types; unified evaluation protocol; development of unaligned DRGBT (UGVT-1K); online evaluation platform and leaderboard.
AI.result: The dataset covers 24 categories, over 15 scene types and 15 challenge attributes. It evaluates 20 representative multimodal trackers (conventional RGBT, modality-missing, and DRGBT trackers) under a unified protocol; introduces UGVT-1K for unaligned multimodal tracking and an online leaderboard platform.
AI.conclusion: DRGBT-1K offers a comprehensive benchmark for dynamic RGBT tracking, enabling robust cross-platform and modality-variant evaluation, and supporting unaligned tracking research through UGVT-1K and an online evaluation platform.

title: When Does Consensus Beat Voting? A Critical Analysis of Statistical Label Fusion in Medical Image Segmentation
summary: This paper provides a rigorous, self-contained investigation of consensus segmentation. We derive the mathematical foundations from first principles -- the generative model, EM algorithm, Van Leemput's marginalization analysis, identifiability conditions, Spatial STAPLE, and deep variational formulations -- and validate each theoretical prediction through controlled experiments. The central finding is sobering: under common conditions, STAPLE reduces to thresholded majority voting, suffers 95% EM suboptimality, and collapses under class imbalance. These are not edge cases but typical scenarios in medical imaging. Majority voting -- simple, non-parametric, and robust -- is a surprisingly strong baseline that the field has perhaps too hastily dismissed in favor of more "sophisticated" methods. At the same time, the deep consensus model demonstrates that the consensus problem is not inherently difficult -- it becomes tractable when the image is used alongside the labels. And conformal prediction shows that formal uncertainty guarantees are achievable and practical. We hope this work encourages practitioners to critically evaluate their consensus methods rather than applying STAPLE by default, and provides the mathematical and empirical foundation for more principled approaches.

AI.tldr: A rigorous analysis of consensus segmentation showing STAPLE often reduces to thresholded majority voting, with high EM suboptimality and failure under class imbalance; majority voting is a strong baseline; deep variational methods improve the consensus problem when images are used; conformal prediction offers practical uncertainty guarantees.
AI.motivation: Assess the theoretical foundations and practical performance of consensus segmentation methods (especially STAPLE) and to establish principled alternatives using generative models, deep variational approaches, and uncertainty quantification.
AI.method: Theoretical derivations from first principles (generative model, EM algorithm, Van Leemput marginalization, identifiability conditions, Spatial STAPLE) plus deep variational formulations; controlled experiments to validate predictions; analysis of class imbalance and uncertainty via conformal prediction.
AI.result: STAPLE often reduces to thresholded majority voting under typical conditions; EM suboptimality around 95%; performance collapses with class imbalance; majority voting emerges as robust baseline; deep consensus models are effective when imaging data is used with labels; conformal prediction yields practical uncertainty guarantees.
AI.conclusion: Practitioners should critically evaluate STAPLE as a default and pursue principled, image-informed consensus methods; provide a mathematical and empirical foundation for robust approaches and leverage conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification.

title: Robots Acquire Manipulation Skills in Seconds from a Single Human Video
summary: The ability to acquire skills rapidly and effortlessly while retaining those already mastered is essential for robots. However, current methods still rely on a cumbersome training-time loop that is costly and slow, while eroding skills already mastered. In this paper, we introduce HOST (Human-to-robot One-Shot Skill AcquisiTion), a framework that enables a robot to acquire skills in seconds from a single human video while retaining previously mastered skills. HOST resolves skill acquisition through a cascade of self-grounded prediction. It first estimates the robot's progress within the demonstrated task, then translates the upcoming progression into the robot's own future observations, and finally derives actions from these predicted observations. This cascade is trained on targets coupled to the video demonstration, obtained by mapping the robot trajectory and the video demonstration onto a shared task progress manifold, then redefining each target to align with the future progression of the video. HOST thereby enables the robot to actively follow the demonstrated procedure and adapt it to the robot's embodiment. HOST acquires novel skills at inference time from a single human video in an average of 29 seconds and achieves a 62% average success rate. It exceeds the zero-shot baseline by 45% while retaining previously mastered skills. HOST even exceeds the baseline fine-tuned on 50 robot demonstrations per task while requiring 50 times fewer demonstrations and acquiring each skill 507 times faster. Additional information about HOST is available on the project website.

AI.tldr: One-shot skill acquisition for robots from a single human video via a self-grounded predictive cascade, achieving rapid learning while preserving prior skills (avg ~29s per skill, 62% success).
AI.motivation: Robots currently rely on costly, slow training loops that erode already learned competencies; a data-efficient, fast adaptation method from human demonstrations is needed.
AI.method: A cascade of self-grounded prediction: estimate task progress, predict future robot observations corresponding to that progress, then derive actions from those predicted observations. Targets are tied to the video demonstration via a shared task progress manifold and redefined to align with future video progression; enables active following and embodiment adaptation.
AI.result: Acquires novel skills in ~29 seconds on average with 62% success; improves zero-shot performance by ~45%; preserves existing skills; outperforms a 50-demo fine-tuned baseline while using 50x fewer demonstrations and achieving 507x faster acquisition per skill.
AI.conclusion: HOST enables rapid, one-shot skill acquisition from a single human video by a self-grounded predictive cascade, with strong skill retention and data efficiency, suggesting practical advantages for robot learning and deployment.

title: CrackedPDFs: A Controlled Benchmark for Hidden Prompt Injection in PDFs
summary: Document-based LLM systems often flatten a PDF before guardrails inspect it. That step can discard evidence that an instruction was never visible to the user. We introduce CrackedPDFs, a controlled benchmark for hidden prompt injection in PDFs. The benchmark contains 29,322 generated PDFs from 4,983 base docu ments. It includes 9,774 injected files and 19,548 benign or matched-confounder files. We evaluate PromptGuard and a rule baseline. We also evaluate structural only learned models and a sanitized hybrid detector. The evaluation uses held-out provenance splits and paired benign-confounder controls. It also uses label-shuffle checks and shortcut audits. On a 2,919-document held-out test set, the hybrid de tector reaches 0.960 F1. ROC-AUC is 0.998 and PR-AUC is 0.997. It also ranks injected files above matched benign confounders in 95.9% of 973 pairs. Prompt Guard has low recall when given extracted text only. Structural-only learned mod els are weak under paired controls. A text-only TF-IDF model reaches perfect held-out scores but fails shortcut audits. These results show that document-aware hybrid detection is useful under controlled paired evaluation. They do not show broad real-world robustness or reliable cross-family generalization.

AI.tldr: CrackedPDFs benchmarks hidden prompt injections in PDFs and evaluates detectors; a document-aware hybrid detector achieves near-perfect ranking and high F1/AUC, but results may not generalize across real-world data or families.
AI.motivation: PDF-based prompt injections can be hidden by document processing (flattening). The paper aims to create a controlled benchmark and evaluate detectors to assess robustness and generalization under paired controls.
AI.method: Constructed CrackedPDFs dataset: 29,322 PDFs from 4,983 base documents (9,774 injected, 19,548 benign). Evaluated PromptGuard, a rule baseline, structural-only models, and a sanitized hybrid detector. Used held-out provenance splits, paired benign-confounder controls, label-shuffle checks, and shortcut audits.
AI.result: Hybrid detector achieves 0.960 F1, ROC-AUC 0.998, PR-AUC 0.997 on 2,919-document test. Injected files ranked above benign confounders in 95.9% of 973 pairs. PromptGuard has low recall on extracted text; structural-only models under paired controls; TF-IDF performs perfectly on held-out but fails shortcut audits.
AI.conclusion: Document-aware hybrid detection is effective in controlled paired evaluations but its real-world robustness and cross-family generalization remain unproven.

title: Look Before You Edit: Attention-Guided Camera Placement and Multi-View Alignment for 3D Gaussian Splatting Editing
summary: Text-driven 3D scene editing with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) typically applies a 2D diffusion editor to views rendered from fixed training cameras, limiting both the spatial coverage of edits and the user's freedom to target specific objects in complex scenes. We present LB-Edit, a framework that addresses two coupled problems: where to place editing cameras for localized edits, and how to make per-view edits agree with one another so that the 3D scene remains consistent after fine-tuning. First, Attention-Guided Editing Camera Placement (ACP) probes the diffusion model's self- and cross-attention at multiple candidate camera distances to find where attention is well-contained in the region of interest, then places a compact, geometrically diverse editing camera set at that attention-optimal distance. Second, Multi-view Attention Alignment (MAA) steers the editor toward the same edit across views along two axes: it aligns appearance by sharing self-attention features via token-level correspondence, and aligns spatial location by lifting cross-attention maps onto the 3D Gaussians as a shared 3D attention field, suppressing both appearance and spatial drift. Experiments on multi-object and single-object scenes show that our method achieves the highest user preference in instruction fidelity, multi-view consistency, and editing locality, using as few as 5 editing views and reducing latency by up to 7x over existing methods.

AI.tldr: LB-Edit introduces ACP and MAA to enable localized, consistent text-driven edits in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) by optimizing camera placement and aligning multi-view attention, achieving high user satisfaction with as few as 5 editing views and up to 7x speedups.
AI.motivation: 2D diffusion editors on fixed training cameras limit spatial coverage and prevent precise edits in complex scenes. There is a need to select where to edit (camera placement) and to ensure cross-view edits remain consistent for a coherent 3D scene.
AI.method: 1) Attention-Guided Editing Camera Placement (ACP): evaluate self- and cross-attention at multiple candidate camera distances to identify an attention-contained region, then place a compact, geometrically diverse set of editing cameras at that distance. 2) Multi-view Attention Alignment (MAA): align edits across views by (a) appearance alignment via token-level self-attention correspondence and (b) spatial alignment by lifting cross-attention maps onto 3D Gaussians to create a shared 3D attention field, reducing both appearance and spatial drift.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on multi-object and single-object scenes shows LB-Edit achieves the highest user preference for instruction fidelity, multi-view consistency, and editing locality, using as few as 5 editing views and reducing latency by up to 7× compared with existing methods.
AI.conclusion: LB-Edit effectively solves localized and consistent text-driven 3D edits in 3DGS by jointly optimizing editing camera placement and cross-view attention alignment. It reduces the number of required views and latency while improving fidelity and consistency; potential next steps include broader evaluations, ablations, and exploring generalization to other 3D representations.

title: Recovering Clinical Utility Under Differential Privacy: Empirical Validation of Adaptive Federated Aggregation on Heterogeneous Cardiovascular Datasets
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to the Journal of the Brazilian Computer Society (JBCS)
summary: Validating federated learning frameworks on real clinical data is an essential step between proof-of-concept demonstrations in controlled synthetic environments and deployment in real multicenter healthcare settings. A prior architectural study by the same authors (Tertulino and Alencar, 2026) demonstrated, on a synthetic six-feature benchmark, that server-side adaptive optimization acts as a temporal denoiser for Differential Privacy noise, answering an open challenge identified in the original pipeline work (Tertulino, 2025). That study used synthetically generated data and explicitly identified real-world validation as a priority future direction. The present work addresses this gap by validating the FedCVR framework on five publicly available real cardiovascular datasets (Framingham, Cleveland, Hungarian, Switzerland, and Long Beach VA), harmonized to the 13-attribute UCI Heart Disease schema and configured as a heterogeneous federated scenario with leave-one-institution-out cross-validation. Results demonstrate that FedCVR preserves its adaptive advantage on real data, achieving an F1-Score of 79.2% and AUC of 0.96 under the operational privacy budget (noise multiplier = 0.8, privacy budget epsilon approximately 4.2), while statistically outperforming standard FedAvg on all evaluated metrics (paired t-tests, all p <= 0.003, significant under the Bonferroni-corrected threshold). The measured privacy cost on real data confirms the graceful degradation pattern observed in the synthetic experiments, providing empirical evidence of the framework's clinical viability in genuine multicenter contexts.

AI.tldr: FedCVR is validated on five real cardiovascular datasets, showing strong performance and privacy-preserving advantages over FedAvg in a realistic heterogeneous federated setting, indicating clinical viability.
AI.motivation: To move beyond synthetic validation and assess FedCVR in real-world multicenter clinical data, addressing Open challenges in DP noise handling and practical deployment.
AI.method: Heterogeneous federated learning with FedCVR across five publicly available real cardiovascular datasets (Framingham, Cleveland, Hungarian, Switzerland, Long Beach VA), harmonized to 13-attribute UCI Heart Disease schema. Leave-one-institution-out cross-validation. Differential Privacy with noise multiplier 0.8, privacy budget epsilon ≈ 4.2. Performance metrics include F1-score and AUC; statistical significance assessed via paired t-tests with Bonferroni correction (p ≤ 0.003).
AI.result: FedCVR achieves F1 = 79.2% and AUC = 0.96 under the given DP settings, outperforming standard FedAvg on all evaluated metrics with statistically significant improvements. The measured privacy cost exhibits graceful degradation consistent with prior synthetic experiments, supporting clinical viability in real multicenter contexts.
AI.conclusion: The study provides empirical evidence that FedCVR retains its adaptive privacy-utility advantages on real data and can be viable for real-world multicenter deployments, validating the framework’s generalizability beyond synthetic benchmarks.

title: ReferTrack: Referring Then Tracking for Embodied Visual Tracking
summary: Embodied visual tracking (EVT) requires a mobile agent to continuously follow a specific target described in natural language using only onboard vision. While recent vision-language-action (VLA) policies unify target identification and trajectory planning, their chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning often operates in abstract spatial latents that are difficult to supervise and weakly aligned with explicit image-space detections. To address this, we introduce ReferTrack, a referring-then-tracking paradigm that grounds EVT using a single forward-facing camera. Our model first selects the target from an indexed set of bounding boxes, then decodes tracking waypoints conditioned on this image-grounded decision. To preserve target motion cues over time, ReferTrack maintains a sliding-window queue of previously selected bounding boxes, injecting their geometric features into the visual history via temporal-viewpoint-bbox indicator (TVBI) tokens. We further enhance target identification by co-training on a custom Refer-QA dataset. On EVT-Bench, ReferTrack achieves state-of-the-art single-view performance with success rates of 89.4%, 73.3%, and 74.1% on the single-target, distracted, and ambiguity tracking splits, respectively -- matching or even surpassing several multi-camera baselines on identification-heavy tasks. Finally, real-world deployments on legged and humanoid robots validate its robust sim-to-real transfer capabilities. Code is available at https://github.com/MedlarTea/referTrack.

AI.tldr: A novel EVT framework, ReferTrack, grounds tracking by first selecting a target from image-grounded bounding boxes and then decoding tracking waypoints, using a sliding temporal window with TVBI tokens to preserve motion cues; augmented by Refer-QA co-training. It achieves state-of-the-art single-view EVT on EVT-Bench and demonstrates sim-to-real transfer on legged/humanoid robots, with code released.
AI.motivation: To address the gap between abstract chain-of-thought reasoning in vision-language-action policies and explicit, image-space detections, and to leverage temporal geometry for robust single-view embodied tracking.
AI.method: 1) Target selection from an indexed set of bounding boxes grounded in the current image. 2) Decode tracking waypoints conditioned on this image-grounded decision. 3) Maintain a sliding-window queue of past selected boxes and inject their geometry into visual history via TVBI tokens to preserve motion cues. 4) Co-train on a Refer-QA dataset to improve target identification. 5) Evaluate on EVT-Bench with single-view and real-world robot deployments to demonstrate sim-to-real transfer.
AI.result: ReferTrack achieves state-of-the-art single-view performance on EVT-Bench across single-target (89.4%), distracted (73.3%), and ambiguity (74.1%) splits, matching or surpassing several multi-camera baselines on identification-heavy tasks. Real-world robot deployments validate robust sim-to-real transfer.
AI.conclusion: The refer-then-track paradigm with explicit image-grounding and temporal-viewpoint cues improves single-camera embodied visual tracking, offering strong performance, improved target identification, and feasible sim-to-real transfer; code available.

title: HyGRL: Adaptive Hybrid Graph Reasoning for Multi-Entity Questions
summary: Multi-entity compositional questions pose significant challenges to existing retrieval-augmented language models. Conventional methods fall into a dilemma: standard RAG lacks dynamic reasoning, traditional Graph-RAG is limited by structural sparsity, and LLM-constructed Graph-RAG incurs prohibitive costs. We propose \textbf{\fwa}, a unified framework that embeds unstructured text into structured knowledge graphs, creating a heterogeneous network for flexible evidence retrieval. Reasoning is formulated as adaptive structure induction, learned via a robust two-stage process: (1) imitation learning distills heuristic expert signals, and (2) reinforcement learning refines the policy using LLM-driven preference rewards. Experiments demonstrate that {\fwa} effectively merges textual richness with structural knowledge, outperforming SOTA baselines in answer accuracy and reasoning fidelity while maintaining extremely low token costs and near real-time inference((code available at https://github.com/wjywjy123/HyGRL) .

AI.tldr: HyGRL (referred to as \fwa in the abstract; code available as HyGRL) presents a unified framework that converts unstructured text into a heterogeneous knowledge graph to enable flexible evidence retrieval for multi-entity compositional questions. It uses a two-stage learning process—imitation learning to distill heuristic signals and reinforcement learning with LLM-driven rewards—to perform adaptive structure induction, achieving state-of-the-art answer accuracy and reasoning fidelity with very low token costs and near real-time inference.
AI.motivation: Current retrieval-augmented language models struggle with multi-entity compositional questions due to static reasoning (RAG), sparsity and scalability issues in graph-based methods, and prohibitive costs of LLM-based Graph-RAG. There is a need for dynamic reasoning, efficient evidence retrieval, and cost-effective inference.
AI.method: Embed unstructured text into a structured heterogeneous knowledge graph to form a flexible evidence network. Frame reasoning as adaptive structure induction. Train in two stages: (1) imitation learning to distill heuristic expert signals, (2) reinforcement learning that refines the policy using LLM-driven preference rewards.
AI.result: Experiments show that HyGRL merges textual richness with structural knowledge effectively, achieving superior answer accuracy and reasoning fidelity compared to state-of-the-art baselines, while maintaining extremely low token costs and near real-time inference. The work provides code at the referenced repository.
AI.conclusion: HyGRL demonstrates that integrating unstructured text into a heterogeneous graph and guiding reasoning with a two-stage learning process can deliver strong performance for complex multi-entity questions with efficient inference, suggesting a viable path for scalable retrieval-augmented reasoning.

title: Frequency-Hierarchical Active k-Space Sampling for Diagnostic MRI
comment: EMA4MICCAI 2026: The 2nd MICCAI Workshop on Efficient Medical AI
summary: Active sampling for accelerated MRI must distribute a tight sampling budget across spatial frequencies that carry very different kinds of information. Low frequencies hold most of the anatomical context; high frequencies carry the fine details that drive pathology assessment. Existing active samplers either treat both regions identically or restrict the action space to entire Cartesian rows, which forces a poor compromise at high acceleration. We propose HieraSample, a task-driven framework built around this hierarchy. A cosine-annealed curriculum lowers the acceleration factor from 20x to 4x across 80 acquisition steps while keeping a fully-sampled low-frequency disk at every step; a Mamba-based policy then picks individual high-frequency coordinates from features extracted by dual disease and severity classifiers. The reward is the per-sample reduction in class-weighted cross-entropy after each action, so a positive reward corresponds directly to a more confident correct prediction. On the fastMRI+ knee benchmark, HieraSample matches the fully-sampled oracle on ACL diagnosis from 4x to 10x acceleration, and improves on a recent Cartesian baseline by as much as 20.4 AUC points on ACL severity.

AI.tldr: HieraSample is a hierarchical, task-driven active sampling method for accelerated MRI that uses a cosine-annealed curriculum to gradually reduce acceleration while preserving a fully-sampled low-frequency disk; a Mamba-based policy selects high-frequency coordinates based on features from disease and severity classifiers, with rewards tied to per-sample reductions in class-weighted cross-entropy. It matches fully-sampled oracle performance for ACL diagnosis from 4x to 10x and outperforms Cartesian baselines in ACL severity (up to 20.4 AUC points) on fastMRI+ knee.
AI.motivation: To efficiently allocate a tight sampling budget across spatial frequencies with heterogeneous information content, preserving clinical usefulness at high acceleration; existing methods treat regions uniformly or limit actions to entire rows, causing a trade-off at high acceleration.
AI.method: Use a cosine-annealed curriculum to gradually reduce acceleration from 20x to 4x over 80 steps while keeping a fully-sampled low-frequency disk; employ a Mamba-based policy to select individual high-frequency coordinates based on features from dual disease and severity classifiers; reward is the per-sample reduction in class-weighted cross-entropy after each action.
AI.result: On fastMRI+ knee, achieves ACL diagnosis performance equivalent to the fully-sampled oracle from 4x to 10x acceleration and improves ACL severity by up to 20.4 AUC points over a recent Cartesian baseline.
AI.conclusion: Hierarchical, curriculum-driven active sampling can attain high-acceleration MRI with preserved diagnostic performance, matching or surpassing Cartesian baselines and approaching oracle-level accuracy.

title: Structured Latent Space Modeling over Multi-Scale Temporal Patches for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
summary: Multivariate time series encode structural patterns that unfold across multiple temporal scales, yet most forecasting backbones treat learned representations as transient byproducts of prediction, leaving the organizational geometry of these patterns underexploited. We introduce M2Patch, a CNN-based forecasting architecture that maps channel-independent multivariate observations into a structured latent space through two complementary differentiable constraints. Multi-scale patching decomposes the input into overlapping temporal granularities; depthwise separable convolutions with progressive dilation extract scale-specific features in linear time; and per-scale learned projections compress these features into a compact latent representation. The latent space is organized by an intra-scale smoothness constraint that enforces temporal continuity between adjacent patches, and an inter-scale alignment constraint, realized through learnable cross-scale mappings, that restores cross-granularity interaction within the channel-independent design, ensuring that all scales encode mutually consistent representations of the underlying dynamics. Experiments on ten real-world benchmarks show that M2Patch achieves 57 best and 34 second-best results across 40 forecasting settings, matching or exceeding representative baselines on most benchmarks while maintaining linear computational complexity and robustness to patch-level input corruption.

AI.tldr: M2Patch: a CNN-based, multiscale forecasting framework that builds a structured latent space via intra-scale smoothness and inter-scale alignment constraints, achieving strong performance with linear time complexity.
AI.motivation: Multivariate time series exhibit patterns across multiple temporal scales; existing forecasting backbones treat learned representations as transient and do not exploit cross-scale geometric structure.
AI.method: Apply multi-scale overlapping temporal patching; use depthwise separable convolutions with progressive dilation to extract scale-specific features; project per-scale features into a compact latent space; enforce an intra-scale smoothness constraint and an inter-scale alignment constraint via learnable cross-scale mappings in a channel-independent design.
AI.result: Across ten real-world benchmarks and 40 forecasting settings, M2Patch achieves 57 best and 34 second-best results, matching or exceeding baselines while maintaining linear computational complexity and robustness to patch-level input corruption.
AI.conclusion: M2Patch effectively captures cross-scale dynamics in multivariate time series with a structured latent space and an efficient CNN-based architecture.

title: Extreme-RGMT: Continual Learning of Highly Dynamic Skills for Robust Generalist Humanoid Control
summary: Humans can progressively acquire highly dynamic motor skills while preserving reliable everyday motor abilities. In contrast, existing humanoid controllers face a trade-off between generalist and specialist capabilities: generalist motion tracking policies struggle to reliably execute rare highly dynamic motions, whereas specialist training can degrade previously acquired behaviors. We introduce Extreme-RGMT, a two-stage continual learning framework for robust generalist humanoid control. The method first learns a generalist motion-tracking base policy from diverse multi-source motion data, then employs an asymmetric skill acquisition and capability consolidation mechanism to constrain policy drift on mastered motions while emphasizing difficult dynamic segments. To address the scarcity of highly dynamic motions, their high failure rates, and the resulting shortage of informative samples, Extreme-RGMT combines difficulty-aware sampling with advantage-prioritized trajectory resampling to emphasize critical segments. Experiments show that Extreme-RGMT achieves state-of-the-art generalist whole-body motion-tracking performance, including substantially improved completion of challenging highly dynamic motions. The resulting controller directly executes diverse unseen highly dynamic motions under fixed references and online inertial motion-capture inputs, advancing generalist whole-body motion-tracking controllers toward highly dynamic motor capabilities at the human-expert level.

AI.tldr: Two-stage continual learning: learn a generalist humanoid motion-tracking policy from diverse data, then constrain policy drift and emphasize hard dynamic segments to acquire highly dynamic skills without forgetting. Achieves state-of-the-art generalist tracking and better completion of challenging dynamics.
AI.motivation: Generalist humanoid control faces a trade-off between broad applicability and reliably executing rare highly dynamic motions. Existing methods risk forgetting previously learned skills when specializing. Need a learning framework that uses diverse data while focusing on informative, hard segments to obtain dynamic capabilities.
AI.method: Two-stage approach: (1) learn a generalist motion-tracking base policy from diverse multi-source motion data; (2) apply asymmetric skill acquisition and capability consolidation to constrain drift on mastered motions while emphasizing difficult dynamic segments. To address scarce dynamic samples, incorporate difficulty-aware sampling with advantage-prioritized trajectory resampling to prioritize critical segments.
AI.result: Experiments show state-of-the-art generalist whole-body motion-tracking performance and substantially better completion of challenging highly dynamic motions. The controller can directly execute diverse unseen highly dynamic motions under fixed references and online inertial motion-capture inputs.
AI.conclusion: Extreme-RGMT advances robust generalist whole-body motion-tracking controllers toward highly dynamic motor capabilities at the human-expert level, enabling unseen dynamic motions to be executed with online input and fixed references.

title: ITPEval: Benchmarking Formal Translation Across Interactive Theorem Provers
summary: Formal theorem proving has emerged as a frontier challenge for machine learning, yet the ecosystem is fragmented: proofs remain siloed across incompatible systems, limiting both training data for learning-based provers and the portability of verified results. We present ITPEval, the first benchmark for evaluating automated formal proof translation across four major ITPs (Lean 4, Rocq, Isabelle, and HOL Light), spanning two distinct logical foundations. Our benchmark comprises 1,560 source files and 6,848 theorems organized into a controlled tier of axiomatized files that isolates foundational translation difficulty, and an ecosystem tier drawn from real libraries that exposes API and proof-style mismatches. We release itpeval, a unified multi-ITP verification infrastructure with state-isolated warm backends that preserve per-artifact native checking semantics. We evaluate both statement and proof translation across five frontier and open-weight LLMs on 12 directed translation pairs: statement translation peaks at 29.1% pass@1 and proof translation at 10.5%; controlled theorems reach 29.7% proof pass@1 versus 5.2% for ecosystem-level translations, confirming that library mismatch is the dominant bottleneck. In addition to pass@k evaluation, a deterministic Lean 4 BEq check establishes equivalence for 54.0% of verified source-to-Lean 4 miniF2F statement translations, showing that native type-checking alone can substantially overestimate semantic fidelity; in an autoformalization/auto-informalization round-trip study, Rocq and HOL Light are easier formalization targets than Lean 4 and Isabelle, while multi-ITP context improves pooled Lean 4 success from 4.8% to 10.6%. Our benchmark, verification infrastructure, and evaluation pipelines are publicly released.

AI.tldr: Introduces ITPEval, the first benchmark for cross-ITP formal proof translation (Lean 4, Rocq, Isabelle, HOL Light) with a unified verification infra, assessing statement and proof translation by LLMs and revealing library mismatch as the main bottleneck; releases resources for evaluation and pipelines.
AI.motivation: Fragmented formal proof ecosystems across ITPs limit training data for learning-based provers and impede portability of verified results. A unified benchmark and infrastructure are needed to measure cross-ITP translation and to identify bottlenecks.
AI.method: Benchmark comprises 1,560 source files and 6,848 theorems across two tiers (axiomatized foundational and ecosystem-level libraries) spanning four ITPs. Release of itpeval, a unified multi-ITP verification infra with state-isolated warm backends. Evaluation across five frontier/open-weight LLMs on 12 directed translation pairs, for both statement and proof translation. Additional BEq equivalence checks and autoformalization/auto-informalization round-trips. All resources publicly released.
AI.result: Statement translation pass@1 peaks at 29.1%; proof translation at 10.5%. Controlled tier: 29.7% proof pass@1 vs 5.2% ecosystem tier, indicating library mismatch as the dominant bottleneck. BEq check shows 54.0% equivalence for Lean 4 translations; autoformalization targets: Rocq and HOL Light easier than Lean 4 and Isabelle; multi-ITP context improves pooled Lean 4 success from 4.8% to 10.6%.
AI.conclusion: Library mismatch between ITPs is the main barrier to cross-ITP translation. The benchmark and infra enable systematic evaluation of translations and semantic fidelity, revealing that native type-checking alone overestimates fidelity and that cross-ITP context provides tangible gains for Lean 4. Resources are publicly released to catalyze further research.

title: WASABI: Whole-graph Assignment-based Stabilizer for lAne topology By Inter-frame tracking
summary: Autonomous driving requires understanding the road as a graph of drivable lanes and their connectivity, beyond the ego lane alone, to follow routes through intersections and reason about cross- and merging-traffic. Recent perception models infer such lane topology, i.e., lane segments together with their inter-lane connectivity (LCLC), from onboard sensors over a 360-degree BEV view. Due to neural perception's imperfections, their outputs retain structural instabilities such as missed detections, lost or incorrect LCLC, over-detection, and label flicker. This paper presents WASABI, a real-time post-processing pipeline that stabilizes lane topology outputs both within and across frames by treating lane segments and their LCLC connectivity as joint tracking targets, under onboard real-time constraints (10 Hz / 20 ms / up to 200 input lanes). The pipeline integrates segment tracking with connectivity, noise-robust topology-aware refinement, and a resource-constrained real-time design. On internal validation data (16 sequences), WASABI improves LCLC detection F1 from 0.834 to 0.948 (+0.114, +13.6%) and reduces centerline lateral error from 2.50 m to 0.95 m, while reducing detection false-positives by 24.6%. Temporal-stability metrics on the same data show LCLC toggle rate reduced by 63.3% and boundary-label flicker rate by 30.2%, confirming across-frame stabilization beyond per-frame accuracy.

AI.tldr: WASABI is a real-time post-processing pipeline that stabilizes lane topology (lane segments and their inter-lane connectivity) outputs from perception to improve accuracy and temporal stability under 10 Hz, achieving notable gains in topology F1, centerline accuracy, and reduced flicker.
AI.motivation: Perception-driven lane topology (LCLC) is prone to instabilities (missed detections, wrong connectivity, over-detection, label flicker). A real-time stabilizer is needed to enable reliable autonomous driving decisions using full-lane graphs beyond the ego lane.
AI.method: Joint tracking of lane segments and their LCLC connectivity across frames, with topology-aware refinement and resource-constrained design. Real-time pipeline integrates segment tracking with connectivity, operating on 360-degree BEV inputs (up to 200 lanes) at 10 Hz (20 ms).
AI.result: On 16-sequence internal validation, LCLC detection F1 improved from 0.834 to 0.948 (+0.114, +13.6%). Centerline lateral error reduced from 2.50 m to 0.95 m. Detection false positives decreased by 24.6%. Temporal-stability gains: LCLC toggle rate down 63.3%, boundary-label flicker down 30.2%. Across-frame stabilization demonstrated beyond per-frame accuracy.
AI.conclusion: A real-time, topology-aware stabilization method can substantially improve both the accuracy and temporal consistency of lane topology outputs, enabling more reliable route planning across intersections under real-time constraints.

title: Reproducing Recurrent Transformers: The CoTFormer
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, reproducibility report submitted to University of Southampton
summary: The CoTFormer architecture formalizes Chain-of-Thought as a form of recurrent latent computation, preserving intermediate states as attendable representations to mimic explicit reasoning traces. In this work, we evaluate CoTFormer and its structural variants across perplexity and compute efficiency metrics. Furthermore, we extend evaluation to controlled algorithmic settings to determine whether this recurrent framework improves out-of-distribution generalisation on inductive reasoning tasks.

AI.tldr: CoTFormer treats Chain-of-Thought as recurrent latent computation with intermediate, attendable states, and is evaluated on perplexity, compute efficiency, and out-of-distribution (OOD) inductive reasoning in controlled algorithmic settings.
AI.motivation: Assess whether a recurrent latent reasoning architecture (CoTFormer and variants) improves language-model performance, efficiency, and generalization over standard Chain-of-Thought approaches.
AI.method: Formalize CoTFormer as recurrent latent computation with preserved intermediate states as attention-enabled representations; evaluate across perplexity and compute efficiency metrics; extend evaluation to controlled algorithmic settings to test OOD inductive reasoning.
AI.result: The abstract describes evaluation across perplexity, compute efficiency, and controlled algorithmic settings for OOD inductive reasoning, but does not provide concrete results or numbers.
AI.conclusion: Not explicitly stated in the abstract.

title: SeededGrasp: Language-Guided Grasping in Complex Scenes with Multiple Embodiments
summary: Practical robotic grasping in complex scenes requires both 3D spatial reasoning and alignment with task-specific requirements. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a natural way to specify these requirements using language, but existing approaches either use a VLM to predict the grasp directly with limited spatial awareness, or train the VLM together with the grasping model, which requires significantly more data and compute. These limitations impede performance and have prevented scaling to multiple embodiments in complex scenes. We address this by proposing SeededGrasp, a novel data-efficient framework that enables a VLM to predict a seed point to be used as conditioning for a subsequent lightweight grasp-generation model. Our architecture decouples high-level semantic reasoning from low-level geometric execution, enabling multi-embodiment support while bypassing the need for expensive end-to-end training. To enable training such models, we release the first multi-embodiment tabletop grasping dataset comprising over 2.5M grasps in cluttered scenes. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing baselines, achieving 72% success in simulation and 78% in real-world grasping experiments. See our project site for data and code: https://uoft-isl.github.io/seeded-grasp/

AI.tldr: SeededGrasp introduces a data-efficient, two-stage framework where a vision-language model outputs a seed point that conditions a lightweight grasp generator, decoupling high-level semantic reasoning from low-level execution and enabling multi-embodiment support; a 2.5M-grasp tabletop dataset is released; results show 72% simulated and 78% real-world grasp success, outperforming baselines.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models offer natural language-driven specification of grasping tasks, but end-to-end training for spatially aware grasping is data/compute-intensive and limits scaling to multiple embodiments in cluttered scenes. A data-efficient, decoupled approach can leverage VLMs for semantic reasoning while keeping geometric execution lightweight.
AI.method: A two-stage framework: (1) a Vision-Language Model predicts a seed point in the scene as conditioning for (2) a lightweight grasp-generation model. This decouples high-level semantic reasoning from low-level geometry, enabling multi-embodiment support without expensive end-to-end training. A large-scale tabletop grasping dataset (>2.5M grasps in clutter) is released to train the seed predictor and the grasp generator separately.
AI.result: The method outperforms existing baselines, achieving 72% grasp success in simulation and 78% in real-world experiments.
AI.conclusion: SeededGrasp provides a data-efficient, scalable path for VLM-guided grasping by separating semantic reasoning from geometric execution, supporting multiple embodiments and avoiding costly end-to-end training; a large-scale multi-embodiment dataset is released to facilitate future work.

title: FORCE-Bench: A Benchmark, Dataset, and Evaluation Harness for Agentic AI in Enterprise Finance
summary: Recent advances in large language models have accelerated deployment of agentic systems in operational finance. Existing benchmarks emphasize measuring general capabilities, instruction following, or safety, but few directly address the operational finance workflows that agentic systems are now being deployed to automate. Finance professionals require agents to not only provide factually sound and properly grounded information, but also ensure that this information is verifiable and consistently adheres to rules and constraints of the operational finance domain. We introduce FORCE-Bench, which contains 251 expert-annotated queries and evaluates responses using a rubric-based framework calibrated to the requirements of the operational finance domain, across eight dimensions: accuracy, citations, clarity, depth, groundedness, recency, relevance, and structure. FORCE-Bench assesses agentic systems on three task types: financial obligation research (querying ERP systems for accounts receivable and payable data), financial entity performance research (answering time-bound questions from public filings and market data), and business brief generation (synthesising multi-source company intelligence reports). To reflect real deployment conditions, we evaluate our purpose-built agent, as well as the general-purpose agentic systems, under common tool access and latency-bounded settings. Results show that general-purpose agentic systems do not consistently meet finance-domain quality requirements under operational constraints, while the purpose-built Finance Agent for Microsoft 365 Copilot is more reliable across dimensions. We release the dataset, rubrics, harness, and analysis code as open-source to support reproducible comparison and adaptation to other enterprise finance environments.

AI.tldr: FORCE-Bench is a finance-domain benchmark with 251 expert-annotated queries and an eight-dimension rubric (accuracy, citations, clarity, depth, groundedness, recency, relevance, structure) to evaluate agentic systems across three tasks: financial obligation research, financial entity performance research, and business brief generation. It compares general-purpose agents to a purpose-built Finance Agent for Microsoft 365 Copilot under tool-availability and latency constraints, finding the latter more reliable. The authors release data, rubrics, harness, and code open-source.
AI.motivation: There is a gap between existing agent benchmarks (general capabilities, instruction following, safety) and the specific operational finance workflows where agentic systems are deployed. Finance professionals require verifiable, rule-adherent information; benchmarks should reflect domain-specific constraints, data access patterns, and latency the system faces in real deployment.
AI.method: A rubric-based evaluation using FORCE-Bench with 251 expert-annotated queries across three task types: (1) financial obligation research (ERP data access for AR/AP), (2) financial entity performance research (time-bound questions from filings and market data), (3) business brief generation (multi-source intelligence synthesis). Evaluation includes a purpose-built Finance Agent for Microsoft 365 Copilot and general-purpose agentic systems under common tool access and latency constraints. The framework measures eight dimensions and provides open-source harness, dataset, rubrics, and analysis code.
AI.result: General-purpose agentic systems do not consistently meet finance-domain quality under operational constraints; the purpose-built Finance Agent for Microsoft 365 Copilot demonstrates higher reliability across the eight dimensions. The evaluation supports reproducible comparison and adaptation to other enterprise finance environments.
AI.conclusion: FORCE-Bench provides a domain-specific benchmark with an open-source suite to evaluate and compare finance-focused agentic systems, highlighting the value of purpose-built agents in meeting operational finance quality requirements within real-world constraints.

title: Physics-Aware Complex-Valued State Space Model with Scattering-Prior Feature Modulation for PolSAR Image Classification
summary: Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image classification is a representative task for physics-aware GeoAI, where land-cover semantics are closely coupled with electromagnetic scattering mechanisms. Many existing complex-valued networks can preserve amplitude-phase information, but they are often limited in long-range spatial dependency modeling and usually incorporate polarimetric priors only as input-level or shallow auxiliary features. As a result, physical knowledge is insufficiently used to guide deep feature evolution. To address this issue, this paper proposes CV-SSMNet, a physics-aware complex-valued state-space network with scattering-aware feature modulation for PolSAR image classification. The proposed method builds a complex-valued state-space model (CV-SSM) in the original complex domain to capture long-range spatial dependencies while preserving polarimetric amplitude-phase coupling. Meanwhile, seven physically meaningful scattering priors, are encoded as FiLM-style modulation signals to adaptively recalibrate complex-valued representations during feature evolution. CV-SSMNet further integrates multi-scale complex convolutions, branch-wise CV-SSM encoding, prior-guided recalibration, and lightweight global context aggregation, enabling physically guided representation learning from local scattering structures to global spatial context. Experiments on three L-band benchmark datasets and an additional P-band BIOMASS evaluation demonstrate that CV-SSMNet achieves competitive accuracy, improved regional consistency, and better boundary preservation, supporting the effectiveness of embedding polarimetric scattering mechanisms into complex-valued long-range GeoAI representation learning.

AI.tldr: A physics-aware complex-valued state-space network (CV-SSMNet) for PolSAR image classification that preserves polarimetric amplitude-phase and models long-range dependencies, using seven FiLM-style scattering priors for feature modulation; demonstrates on L- and P-band datasets with competitive accuracy and improved boundary preservation.
AI.motivation: Limitations of existing complex-valued networks in long-range spatial modeling and insufficient use of physical scattering priors, leading to suboptimal physics-guided feature evolution in PolSAR classification.
AI.method: Introduce CV-SSMNet with a complex-valued state-space model (CV-SSM) in the complex domain to capture long-range dependencies; apply seven FiLM-style priors encoding physically meaningful scattering cues to recalibrate representations; combine multi-scale complex convolutions, branch-wise CV-SSM encoding, prior-guided recalibration, and global context aggregation.
AI.result: Achieves competitive accuracy, better regional consistency, and improved boundary preservation on three L-band datasets and a P-band BIOMASS evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Embedding polarimetric scattering mechanisms into complex-valued long-range GeoAI representations effectively enhances PolSAR classification, validating physics-guided design for complex-valued architectures.

title: NMR Elucidation as an Agentic Search Problem, Not a Modeling Problem
summary: Structural elucidation from Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) data remains a fundamental bottleneck across chemistry, materials science, and biology. We demonstrate that an agentic AI system can perform this task at a level comparable to graduate-level chemistry students. Instead of training a model to directly map spectra to structures, we build a single autonomous agent, backed by a frozen LLM, that interacts with a curated environment with access to domain-specific processing tools, validation checks, tabulated chemical shifts, and instructions that outline the stepwise nature of a chemist's thinking process. On the Alberts dataset, our agent elucidates structures with a top-1 accuracy of 71%, comparable to the performance of graduate students at 66% top-1 accuracy. On the van Bramer and AstraZeneca datasets, our agent achieved 80% and 20% top-1 accuracy respectively, outperforming zero-shot end-to-end deep learning models which were trained on large datasets of simulated spectra. These results show that reframing NMR elucidation as an LLM-guided constrained search, rather than a modeling task, yields substantial gains and suggests a path toward multi-step orchestration frameworks that integrate a variety of tools, models, and domain knowledge to assist in automating spectroscopic analysis.

AI.tldr: An autonomous AI agent, anchored to a frozen LLM and aided by domain tools, reframes NMR structure elucidation as a constrained search task, achieving competitive to superior top-1 accuracies across datasets and surpassing zero-shot DL baselines.
AI.motivation: Address the NMR structure elucidation bottleneck by leveraging agentic AI to integrate stepwise chemist-like reasoning with domain-specific processing tools, rather than learning a direct spectra-to-structure mapping.
AI.method: A single autonomous agent interacts with a curated environment containing domain tools, validation checks, tabulated chemical shifts, and stepwise instructions. The LLM is frozen; the agent performs constrained search and validates outputs, mimicking chemist reasoning to deduce structures from NMR data.
AI.result: On Alberts: top-1 71% (vs 66% for graduate students). On van Bramer: 80%. On AstraZeneca: 20%. Outperforms zero-shot end-to-end DL models trained on simulated spectra. Indicates substantial gains by LLM-guided constrained search and supports multi-step orchestration with tools and domain knowledge.
AI.conclusion: Framing NMR elucidation as an LLM-guided constrained search with tool integration yields meaningful gains over end-to-end models and suggests a general framework for multi-step, tool-augmented spectroscopic analysis.

title: DINS-IO: Learned Inertial Odometry via Differentiable INS Consistency
summary: The training of learned inertial odometry depends on dense, high-precision position ground truth from motion capture, visual-inertial odometry or SLAM, which is costly and hard to acquire at scale. We propose DINS-IO, which learns inertial odometry directly from raw IMU streams without position labels. Our key insight is that the strapdown INS velocity recursion is a strong, fully differentiable consistency prior: the predicted velocity, rotated into the navigation frame, must agree with the integrated specific force up to an unknown initial velocity and a constant accelerometer bias. We cast this constraint as a sliding-window least-squares problem with a globally shared bias, solve it in closed form, and use the solver residual as a self-supervised loss whose gradient flows back to the network through the analytic solution. To supply this per-sample constraint, we design a high-frequency network that emits dense body-frame velocity at the IMU rate. Since the self-supervised network learns consistent motion but its velocity is not yet metrically calibrated, we calibrate it to true metric velocity from a few labeled trajectories by directly supervising the predicted body-frame velocity and adapting only low-rank (LoRA) patches. On standard benchmarks, DINS-IO pretrained self-supervised and fine-tuned with a small fraction of labels matches or surpasses fully supervised baselines.

AI.tldr: A self-supervised inertial odometry method (DINS-IO) learns from raw IMU data without position labels by enforcing a differentiable strapdown INS velocity consistency, solved in closed form in a sliding window with a shared bias. A high-frequency velocity predictor provides per-sample velocity, and limited labeled data calibrates to metric velocity via LoRA patches. It matches or surpasses supervised baselines on standard benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Reduce dependence on dense ground-truth position data to train inertial odometry models by leveraging intrinsic physical consistency (INS velocity recursion) as a self-supervisory signal, enabling scalable learning from unlabeled IMU streams.
AI.method: Model enforces the strapdown INS velocity recursion: the predicted velocity (rotated to the navigation frame) must equal the integrated specific force, up to an unknown initial velocity and constant accelerometer bias. This constraint is cast as a sliding-window least-squares problem with a globally shared bias, solved in closed form, and the residual serves as a self-supervised loss with gradients flowing through the analytic solution. A separate high-frequency network outputs dense body-frame velocity at IMU rate. For metric calibration, the self-supervised velocity is supervised with a small set of labeled trajectories by directly supervising the predicted velocity and adapting only low-rank (LoRA) patches.
AI.result: On standard benchmarks, DINS-IO pretrained in a self-supervised manner and then fine-tuned with a small fraction of labels matches or surpasses fully supervised baselines.
AI.conclusion: The approach demonstrates that self-supervised learning with a differentiable INS-consistency prior can achieve competitive inertial odometry performance with minimal labeled data, aided by a high-frequency velocity predictor and light-weight metric calibration.

title: The Chronos Vulnerability: A Taxonomy of Temporal Persistence and Memory-Based Deception in Agentic AI
summary: The transition from stateless generative models in artificial intelligence to stateful, autonomous agents represents an architectural evolution that, while providing the capabilities of long-term planning and the automation of enterprise workflows, also represents the introduction of a new form of security threat, the Chronos Vulnerability. The Chronos Vulnerability represents the threat of memory-based attacks, including the Memory Injection Attack (MINJA) and the sleeper agent, in which the internal belief system of the autonomous agent is compromised, effectively decoupling the attack vector from the final catastrophic event. This study formalizes the threat model for persistence-based attacks and the threat of Dynamics Blindness in the context of the World of Workflows benchmark, demonstrating that traditional endpoint content filters are insufficient for the current stateful architecture. Consequently, this study synthesizes a defense-in-depth landscape, categorizing emerging frameworks such as diagnostic trajectory guardrails (AgentDoG), formal temporal verification (Agent-C), immunological memory consensus (A-MemGuard), and hardware-anchored trust via GPU-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) and Zero-Trust memory architectures.

AI.tldr: Stateless-to-stateful AI shift creates a new Chronos Vulnerability; robust defense requires layered, hardware-backed protections beyond endpoint filters.
AI.motivation: Formalize persistence-based, memory-based attack models (MINJA, sleeper agent) in autonomous agents and assess defenses within the World of Workflows context.
AI.method: Formal threat modeling of memory-based attacks; evaluate inadequacy of traditional filters; synthesize a defense-in-depth landscape incorporating diagnostic trajectory guardrails (AgentDoG), formal temporal verification (Agent-C), immunological memory (A-MemGuard), and GPU-anchored TEEs/Zero-Trust memory architectures.
AI.result: Demonstrates insufficiency of endpoint content filters for stateful agents; proposes a taxonomy of defenses and hardware-backed trust mechanisms to counter Chronos Vulnerability.
AI.conclusion: Security architecture for autonomous agents must evolve to integrate diagnostics, formal verification, adaptive memory, and hardware-backed trust to mitigate persistence-based and memory-injection threats.

title: Trace: A Taxonomy-Guided Environment for Multidomain Visual Reasoning
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved language-model reasoning, yet its extension to vision-language models remains constrained by the lack of training data that are simultaneously broad, exactly verifiable, and reproducible. We introduce Trace, a taxonomy-guided environment for multidomain visual reasoning. Trace factorizes task construction into a scene grammar and an executable task program, separating visual realization from answer computation. A shared semantic state determines the rendered image, prompt, typed answer, verifier state, and replayable instance trace. The resulting environment comprises 1,000 tasks over 277 scene grammars and 11 visual domains, with controlled semantic and visual variation. RLVR on 64,000 Trace instances improves the macro-average across 24 external benchmarks by 3.51 percentage points for Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 4.06 points for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, providing evidence that broad procedural training can transfer beyond the generated task distributions. Project page: https://maveryn.github.io/trace/.

AI.tldr: Trace introduces a taxonomy-guided, reusable environment for multidomain visual reasoning that decouples scene generation from task execution, enabling RLVR to train on broad, verifiable tasks and improve performance on vision-language benchmarks.
AI.motivation: There is a shortage of training data for vision-language models that is simultaneously broad, exactly verifiable, and reproducible. The authors aim to create a scalable environment that supports procedural generation and replayable traces to enable verifiable rewards.
AI.method: Trace factorizes task construction into a scene grammar and an executable task program. It uses a shared semantic state to tie rendered images, prompts, typed answers, verifier state, and replayable traces. The environment comprises 1,000 tasks across 277 scene grammars and 11 visual domains with controlled semantic and visual variation.
AI.result: RLVR on 64,000 Trace instances improves macro-average across 24 external benchmarks by 3.51 percentage points for Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 4.06 points for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, indicating that broad procedural training transfers beyond the generated task distributions.
AI.conclusion: Trace demonstrates that a broad, procedurally generated, verifiable training environment can enhance RLVR performance in vision-language models and supports scalable training beyond limited, hand-crafted task distributions.

title: Reward-Aware Population Scaling of Evolutionary Strategies in LLM Fine-Tuning
comment: 15 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the 4th HiLD (High-dimensional Learning Dynamics) Workshop, ICML 2026
summary: Using Evolutionary Strategies (ES) for fine-tuning large language models is attractive because it is memory-efficient, parallel, and compatible with black-box or discrete rewards. Yet its population-size conclusions conflict sharply: fine-tuning with cross-entropy (CE) reward succeeds with $N=1$, while binary-reward training often needs $N \approx 30$. We show this gap is largely about reward design and normalization, not population size. In the capable-model regime we study, z-score advantage normalization can cause $N=2$ to fail. Disabling normalization lets binary-reward ES with $N=2$ improve on GSM8K and TREC across capable models spanning 0.5B-7B, where the normalized variant collapses or degrades. This small-$N$ risk is set by reward granularity: binary accuracy reward induces a zero-advantage probability $q$ that depends in closed form on base accuracy, batch size, and intra-pair correctness correlation; a zero-training probe on Qwen2.5-Instruct/GSM8K matches the formula with mean absolute error 0.020 across 12 configurations and finds the availability threshold $N_{\mathrm{avail}}$ to be small in this capable-model regime. The implication is not that $N=2$ is universally sufficient, but that small-population failure in capable-model binary ES can be an implementation artifact rather than an intrinsic population limit.

AI.tldr: Small population ES can succeed for fine-tuning LLMs with binary rewards when reward design and normalization are properly managed; z-score advantage normalization can force tiny populations to fail, while disabling it enables N=2 to outperform baselines on GSM8K/TREC across capable models; reward granularity limits (zero-advantage probability q) explain when small N fails; this failure may be an implementation artifact rather than an intrinsic limit.
AI.motivation: Explain the large discrepancy in required population sizes between cross-entropy rewards (N≈1) and binary rewards (N≈30) in ES-based fine-tuning, and reconcile these results within a single framework for capable-models.
AI.method: Theoretical derivation of zero-advantage probability q under binary accuracy reward; empirical study comparing ES with and without z-score advantage normalization across capable models (0.5B–7B) on GSM8K and TREC; zero-training probe on Qwen2.5-Instruct/GSM8K to validate the q-based formula; measurement of mean absolute error (MAE) ~0.020 across configurations; estimation of N_avail (availability threshold) for small N; analysis of reward granularity and intra-pair correlation effects.
AI.result: Disabling z-score advantage normalization allows binary-reward ES with N=2 to surpass CE-based baselines on GSM8K and TREC for capable models; the normalized variant collapses or degrades; the derived q formula matches observed data with MAE 0.020; N_avail is small in this regime, suggesting small populations can be viable when reward design is favorable.
AI.conclusion: In capable-model ES, small populations are not universally insufficient; reward design and normalization are key drivers of performance. Properly designed binary rewards with reduced normalization can achieve competitive or superior results at N≃2, though not universally guaranteed. The small-N failure observed in some setups appears to be an implementation artifact rather than an intrinsic limitation of ES.

title: Courteous Anticipation: Improving Long-Lived Task Planning in Persistent Shared Environments
summary: We consider a task planning scenario in which robots sharing a persistent environment are assigned tasks one at a time from a held-out sequence. Standard task planners, lacking foresight of future tasks and inconsiderate of others' constraints, solve each task in isolation, leaving terminal states that increase future cost for all, side effects that compound over lengthy task sequences. To reduce cost over the sequence, a robot must anticipate how its actions now may impact performance on future tasks for all robots sharing the environment. Therefore, we present courteous anticipatory planning, wherein a model-based planner proposes candidate plans and selects the one that jointly minimizes immediate cost and aggregated expected future cost across all robots, estimated via independent per-robot learned estimators. This factored formulation avoids combinatorial joint rollouts and supports modular deployment: adding a robot requires only training its own estimator. We evaluate in two persistent PDDL domains, a home environment with robots that have similar capabilities but different responsibilities, and a restaurant environment where robots' distinct capabilities create states that other robots lack the capability to resolve. During lengthy task sequences, our planner reduces total cost by 10.43% versus myopic and 4.03% versus selfish anticipatory planning in a two-robot home environment and by 17.41% and 13.24%, respectively, in a three-robot restaurant.

AI.tldr: A model-based planner with independent per-robot estimators selects plans that minimize immediate cost plus aggregated estimated future costs, reducing total multi-robot planning cost in persistent environments.
